title: Mohe zhiguan (The Great Calming and Contemplation)

attribution.tradition: Lectures of Zhiyi recorded and edited by his disciple Guanding

summary: Zhiyi's systematic treatise on calming and contemplation (zhiguan) in the perfect-sudden mode, including the six identities (liuji) by which every stage is identical with awakening, the four samādhis and the ten modes of contemplation.
notes: Minimal entry by U51 for the six-identities teachings; the owner of lin:tiantai (U54) should complete it.

title: Pusa yingluo benye jing (Sūtra of the Original Acts that Adorn the Bodhisattva)

attribution.scholarly: Widely regarded as composed in China (5th c.)

summary: Sets out the forty-two stages of the worthies and sages (ten abodes, ten practices, ten dedications, ten grounds, equal and wondrous awakening), preceded by the ten faiths, with six 'natures' (gotra) of practitioners; also bodhisattva precepts.

title: Himitsu mandara jūjūshinron (Treatise on the Ten Abodes of Mind of the Secret Maṇḍala)

structure.description: 10 fascicles; Taishō T2425, vol. 77 (not in the local CBETA range)

summary: Kūkai's classification of minds and teachings into ten ascending abodes, from the animal-like mind to the secret, adorned mind of the Shingon maṇḍala; condensed in the Hizō hōyaku.
notes: Minimal entry by U51; owner of lin:shingon (U55) should complete. Text not available locally; the stage names are given from memory.
